specification.problem: Grover search for a single marked item |w> among N=2^n as evolution under H=|w><w|+|s><s|, |s>=H^{(x)n}|0>. Compare a first-order Lie-Trotter discretisation (power-law error in query count) with maximal-step reflections (dt=pi, exact Grover iterates). The error is 1 - P(w).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance n=3 (N=8), one marked string w, black-box oracle O=I-2|w><w| used once per Grover or Trotter step. Build (A) a Trotter circuit with m steps of step size dt=T/m, and (B) k plain Grover iterations with k=round(pi/(4 theta)-1/2). Measure the n search qubits. The fixed-point/recursive scheme with eps_{j+1}=eps_j^3 and the Chebyshev/Yang phase schedule is out of scope: the abstract does not specify it and its phases are not invented here.

symbols.meaning: number of Trotter steps (= number of oracle queries if the oracle is used as a pi-phase reflection)

equations.label: Two-projector Hamiltonian
equations.description: Hamiltonian whose evolution realises Grover search; the abstract only states that Grover is cast as a Hamiltonian evolution.
equations.abstract_quote: Grover’s quantum search algorithm is described as a Hamiltonian evolution problem.
equations.justification: The specific two-projector form is the standard choice recalled from background knowledge, not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Lie-Trotter step
equations.description: First-order product formula; its error is polynomial in dt, so it is a power law in the step count.
equations.abstract_quote: the computational complexity has a power-law dependence on error when a straightforward Lie-Trotter discretisation formula is used
equations.justification: The power-law claim is stated in the abstract; the explicit product form is standard.
assumptions: the oracle supplies e^{-i dt|w><w|} only for dt=pi, so non-pi steps need an extra construction, e.g. a controlled-phase built from oracle queries (assumption)

equations.label: Reflections at dt=pi
equations.latex: e^{-i\pi|w\rangle\langle w|}=I-2|w\rangle\langle w|=O,\quad e^{-i\pi|s\rangle\langle s|}=I-2|s\rangle\langle s|=-D
equations.description: At the maximal step each factor is an exact reflection. With D=2|s><s|-I=H^n(2|0><0|-I)H^n, the Grover iterate is G=D*O up to a global sign.
equations.abstract_quote: it becomes logarithmic in error when reflection operators are used
equations.justification: A direct identity for dt=pi; the abstract says only that reflection operators are used.

equations.label: Grover rotation success probability
equations.description: Exact success probability after k iterations of G, used for the reflection arm.

equations.label: Trotter error scaling (to fit)
equations.description: Power-law error to be fitted numerically; p and C are not stated in the abstract.
equations.justification: Only the qualitative power-law claim is available.
assumptions: exponent p is determined by simulation

registers.name: search
registers.role: search register, little-endian; the counts key is reversed to read w

registers.name: anc
registers.role: optional ancilla for the multi-controlled phase flip, returned to |0>

specification.initial_state: |0>^n, then H on every search qubit to give |s>

steps.description: Prepare |s> with H on all search qubits.
Arm B: apply k times O (black-box placeholder, one query each) then D = H^n X^n (multi-controlled Z) X^n H^n.

Arm A: apply m Trotter steps with dt=T/m. The phase factor about |s> is done with H^n, X^n, a multi-controlled phase, X^n and H^n. The factor about |w> must come from oracle queries (assumed construction).
Measure the search qubits, compute the error 1-P(w), and compare the two arms at equal query counts.

specification.measurement: Measure the n search qubits into n classical bits. In Qiskit counts the rightmost character is bit 0, so reverse the string before comparing with w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P(w) from counts or the statevector, set error=1-P(w), and tabulate error versus queries for both arms.
assumptions: Scope chosen by the researcher: n=3, single marked item, known count
The oracle is a phase-flip placeholder, with an ancilla if needed
The Trotter arm's non-pi oracle rotations need an unspecified construction
Exponential error control would require fixed-point or phase-generalised reflections, which are not constructed here
missing_information: Exact Hamiltonian normalisation and evolution time used in the paper
